# CosmosDB Documents

CosmosDB is a document based "schemaless" database where all documents are stored in JSON format. While Cosmos supports the ability to use multiple "Containers" per database, Licensify currently uses a single container. This single container approach was chosen due to its perceived simplicity and due to the lack of need for separate container level configs (like which field to use as the partition key) across our document types. If the need every arises, we can migrate whichever documents needed into a new container and make the necessary updates to the code to support multiple containers.

 Despite the schemaless nature of CosmosDB, Licensify does have a defined internal schema for each object type we store. We distinguish between types by using specific partition key patterns. This partition key pattern is documented on each schema linked below.

In order to achieve the best query and read performance, it is important to choose partition keys that will lead to the fewest cross partition queries as well as support healthy horizontal scaling. It is equally important to use partition keys and IDs that are deterministic such that the full partition key and ID are known prior to performing the lookup of a unique document so that Cosmos DB can perform a "point read" (the most efficient way to retrieve a document). See [Partitioning and horizontal scaling in Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/partitioning-overview) for additional info. In order to achieve these goals in the most flexible way possible, we've chosen to use a field called "Partition Key" as our partition key which can be set to any value of our choosing with our application logic. Our partition keys and ids are almost entirely composed of interpolated values that are found elsewhere in a given document. While this leads to these values appearing parseable for meaning, we get the cleanest code and most flexility by not storing any data solely in either of these fields.

When looking at the sample documents, you'll notice that some of the fields in the schema are prefixed with an underscore. These are system fields that are automatically generated by CosmosDB. The field most relevant to us is `_etag` which we use for optimistic concurrency control, if the `_etag` has changed when we perform an update CosmosDB returns a 409 conflict error which lets us know we should pull the latest version of the document and then apply our changes again.
